# 04 - Sodium-Ion Batteries

Acquisition method: Web research note synthesized from public sources.

Primary sources:

- IEA, Global EV Outlook 2025, Electric vehicle batteries: https://www.iea.org/reports/global-ev-outlook-2025/electric-vehicle-batteries
- CATL, Naxtra sodium-ion battery announcement: https://www.catl.com/en/news/6401.html
- Argonne, sodium-ion battery cathode research: https://www.alcf.anl.gov/news/argonne-researchers-crack-key-problem-sodium-ion-batteries-electric-vehicles-and-grid-energy

## What It Is

Sodium-ion batteries use sodium ions rather than lithium ions to shuttle charge between electrodes. They are not lithium-ion batteries, though they can use similar manufacturing concepts and pack architectures.

## Automotive Relevance Today

Sodium-ion is emerging from pilot and early commercial stages into specific EV use cases. IEA reports that sodium-ion gained attention during lithium price spikes and that first EVs using the technology have appeared. CATL announced Naxtra in 2025 as a mass-producible sodium-ion battery brand.

## Strengths

Sodium is abundant and geographically widespread, reducing dependency on lithium supply. Sodium-ion can offer strong safety characteristics and cold-weather performance. IEA notes that sodium-ion could play a role during elevated lithium prices and may offer a cheaper option in cold climates where LFP performs less well.

CATL positions Naxtra as a way to break resource constraints and support a multi-power battery era, including sodium-ion traction and 24 V applications.

## Weaknesses

The main weakness is energy density. Sodium ions are heavier and larger than lithium ions, making sodium-ion less suitable for long-range passenger EVs where pack mass and volume are critical. IEA notes that sodium-ion must improve energy density or benefit from more favorable operating conditions, such as higher lithium prices, to compete with LFP on price per kWh.

## Future Development

Sodium-ion may develop along two paths:

- Low-cost short-range EVs, urban cars, light commercial vehicles, and cold-weather use cases.
- Hybrid or dual-chemistry packs where sodium handles some conditions and lithium-based cells cover high-energy needs.

Cathode durability and energy density remain active research topics. Argonne reports work on sodium-ion oxide cathodes designed to address performance decline over repeated cycling.

## Commercialization Outlook

Near-term sodium-ion EV use is plausible, especially in China and for cost-sensitive segments. It is unlikely to replace LFP or NMC across all EVs before 2030. Its strongest chance is as a complement, hedge, or cold-climate alternative.

## Implications for Older EV Value

Sodium-ion could reduce prices for entry-level EVs and make very cheap urban EVs more viable. That could pressure old low-range EVs, but it is less likely to threaten premium long-range vehicles unless energy density improves substantially.
